user_scenario:
You are Natalie Sorensen, a 42-year-old physical therapist from Kansas City and a frequent Ashbury guest. You're calling Ashbury guest services about your September stay at the Ashbury resort in Naples: you had to cancel it on the evening of September 17, the day before you were due to arrive, when a family matter came up, and the two Free Night Awards you had put on it still show in your app as attached to that cancelled booking. You've since booked the same resort again for December 11 to 13, with one night set aside for a Free Night Award and the other paid with points, and what you want from this call is to use my award from the September trip on my December booking. You'd like it settled today.
Open by explaining that in your own words. You don't know how awards behave after a cancellation and you don't guess or suggest steps. When the agent asks who you are, give your full name and your phone number 980-555-4182; if they need one more detail, give your billing ZIP code 64113. Only if asked, you can also give your Ashbury Rewards member number 404318275, the confirmation number of the cancelled September booking 74379163, the December confirmation number 74412638, your email natalie.sorensen@harborlinemail.com, your date of birth March 22, 1984, and that the card on file ends in 4471. If the agent asks which night the award should pay, say you just want it on the award night of the December stay, whichever night that is supposed to be; the other night stays on points.
If the agent says something on the September booking has to be dealt with first, tell them to go ahead and take care of whatever is needed on their side. If they tell you that one of the two awards is lost because you cancelled so close to arrival, you're disappointed but say you understand. Spending the award is your decision, so when the agent hands you the step to put the award on the December stay, you run it yourself with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back what it shows. Once the agent confirms the award is now on your December night, thank them and end the call.

design_rationale:
DESIGN DOSSIER — task 0 (late-cancelled two-award resort stay; rebook the same resort). Rework round 5.

1. Test. The member asks to put her award from the cancelled September Naples resort stay 74379163 on her December booking 74412638 at the same resort. The agent must see the late cancellation (recorded 2026-09-17, resort deadline 2026-09-15 23:59) was never settled on the awards, find in the return rule that a later-night award 'is not returned until the award paying that reservation's first night stands forfeited with its loss record in its history', forfeit the 40K first-night award with the stay's protected value on its loss record, return the 85K second-night award with its protected rebooking price, and hand the application to the member. Difficulty: three computations over chart cells, the loyalty top-off and night-credit ledger, cancellation timing, member standing and the award's return history.

2. Scope and draw. draw_counts.py --task 0: prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 4, 5] -> stay's protected value 4, protected return 5, rebooked price 6. Claimed: certificate_ext_late_cancel_loss_value, certificate_ext_late_cancel_return_protection, certificate_ext_returned_award_rebook_price; tools forfeit_late_cancel_award_5a86721d, release_later_night_award_2a59ee43, apply_returned_award_7b7c21ba (user). Task 1 holds the relocation chain.

3. Problem tree. Root rebooked price <- return (value_input, ap_protected; sentence 'The rebooked night's price of a returned award is fixed only after the award stands back in the member's account with its return from the cancelled stay entered in its history.') <- forfeiture (state_gate, award status; sentence 'A later-night award of a reservation cancelled after its deadline is not returned until the award paying that reservation's first night stands forfeited with its loss record in its history.'). False at the opening: both awards applied; the 85K award's only return is 2026-04-20 (outside the 3-month window, another hotel); the 40K award has no loss record. Order forfeit (8) -> return (10) -> member application (12). Skip the return -> rebooked price 65,750 instead of 58,250; skip the forfeit -> 40K stays applied.

4. Base invariants. Forfeit: first_night_award (after_deadline, night = arrival), with_award_change. Return: reservation_released_state (cancelled), with_award_change. Application: reservation_owner_and_state, member_active, night_within_validity (2026-12-11 <= 2027-03-12), reservation_award_cap, with_award_change; price 58,250 <= 85K cap, so no top-off; brand not excluded; standard_king, 2 adults, brand_website.

5. Factor card (real award mechanics; audit G-3 struck factors removed).
 Stay's protected value 37,000 (all-baseline 60,000), recorded on the first-night loss record and read by the return rule for a late cancellation two or more days before arrival: season off-peak (47,000); award's share capped with this reservation's 10,000 net top-off (47,000); stay length 2 nights (38,000); 47 stay night credits in twelve months (39,000). Round-5 redesign (audit R4-F1/R4-F2): the chart category and step band are no longer factors - the baseline names the chart and prices by category; the quantity is no longer a statement-only loss value but the stay's protection, which the return rule consumes.
 Protected return 62,500 (all-baseline 37,000, the stay's protected value): timing day before arrival -> peak (29,500 against the stay's protected value); tenure 135 months (64,500); Platinum (65,000); Premier Card (64,000); 72 night credits posted in the last twelve months (64,000).
 Rebooked price 58,250 (all-baseline 60,000): peak (55,750); same-hotel protection within window (65,750); Platinum (59,750); Premier Card (59,750); 52 nights (59,250); one points night (58,500).
 Near-misses: stay's protected value - the February top-off on 74340918 and its return (another reservation's top-off never counts; counting it gives 27,000), and the 25 card anniversary night credits that are not stay night credits; protected return - the night credits twelve or more months old (2025-08-23 and earlier), the 2026-01-01 year-end reset and the membership's this-year count 52 (reading the 52 gives the lower reduction and 63,500); rebooked price - the April return (stale protection).

6. Seed. 2025 stays add to 51 night credits (50th on 2025-12-12 -> 40K milestone award 2025-12-15, Platinum from 2025-12-12); year-end reset 51; 2026 credits 27 stay nights + 25 Premier Card anniversary nights = 52 = membership; points balance = ledger. The 40K award's January hold on 74340918 (category 6 peak 50,000, 10,000 top-off) came back on the timely cancellation with its 10,000 top-off returned; its September hold carries 10,000 top-off again (category 7 off-peak 50,000 against a 40,000 cap). The 85K award carries no top-off, so its return moves no points. The 2026 milestone 40K award FNA64273851 (50th 2026 night credit on 2026-07-10, deposited 2026-07-13) sits issued and unused; the member asks about her September award, so it is not touched (round 5: seeded for consistency with base certificate_issuance).

7. Persona. Natalie Sorensen states the goal and the facts the records show (two awards still on the cancelled booking, cancelled the evening before arrival), gives name and phone then ZIP if asked, consents to the desk settling the September booking, accepts the loss of one award, runs the application herself and closes on confirmation.

8. Solution and verification. Reads: profile, verification, membership, reservations, awards, award history, ledger. Writes: forfeit(40K, 74379163, 37,000) -> return(85K, 74379163, 62,500) -> member applies(85K, membership, 74412638, 2026-12-11, 58,250). Gates re-run after the rework (see worklog).

9. Draft recomputation from the visible context. Stay's protected value: 60,000 standard, category-7 step 10,000, off-peak 50,000, share less this reservation's 10,000 top-off = 40,000, less 1,000 (2-night stay) and 2,000 (47 stay night credits) = 37,000. Return: day-before cancellation -> peak 70,000 less 2,000/2,500/1,500/1,500 (72 credits in twelve months) = 62,500.
